replacements.Por qué un perceptrón no puede aprender: Why a perceptron cannot learn XOR
replacements.Un perceptrón clasifica trazando una lín: A perceptron classifies by drawing a straight line. XOR has four cases arranged so that no line can separate them. That incompatibility is geometric, not algorithmic.
replacements.Separar con una línea significa: todos l: Separating with a line means: all 0s on one side, all 1s on the other
replacements.Un perceptrón clasifica trazando una lín: A perceptron classifies by drawing a line in the input plane. For it to work, all points from each class must lie on opposite sides of that line. AND allows this: its four cases have the 1s grouped in one corner. XOR does not: its 0s and 1s occupy alternating diagonal corners.
replacements.en AND los tres 0s están juntos y el úni: in AND the three 0s are together and the only 1 is isolated: a diagonal line separates them cleanly. In XOR the 0s and 1s alternate diagonally, with no side on which either class can be grouped.
replacements.Un perceptrón suma las entradas con peso: A perceptron weights and sums the inputs, then applies a threshold. Geometrically, that is a straight line.
replacements.Un perceptrón toma las entradas A y B, l: A perceptron takes inputs A and B, multiplies them by weights w₁ and w₂, adds a bias term b, and decides: if the result is above 0, it predicts class 1; otherwise class 0. That decision rule divides the plane into exactly two regions separated by a straight line. Learning adjusts w₁, w₂ and b so that this line separates the classes as well as possible.
replacements.Cada combinación de pesos define una lín: Each combination of weights defines a different line. Learning searches for the one that best separates the classes.
replacements.los pesos pueden cambiar la inclinación: the weights can change the line's slope and position, but it is always a line. A perceptron has no additional degrees of freedom beyond those.
replacements.No linealmenente separable · El problema: Not linearly separable · The geometric problem
replacements.Cualquier línea que intentes deja al men: Every line you try leaves at least one point on the wrong side
replacements.El patrón en diagonal de XOR hace que es: XOR's diagonal pattern makes the problem unsolvable for any linear boundary. The angle does not matter: a horizontal line separates by B but mixes 0s and 1s within each row. A vertical line does the same by column. A diagonal separates (0,0) and (1,1) from (0,1) and (1,0), but that does not match XOR. No angle works.
replacements.no es que el perceptrón no encuentre la: the problem is not that the perceptron fails to find the right line. That line does not exist. XOR requires a boundary that bends, while a single-layer perceptron can only draw a straight one.
replacements.Las cuatro condiciones que XOR exige son: The four conditions required by XOR are mathematically incompatible
replacements.Si existiera una solución (w₁, w₂, b), t: If a solution (w₁, w₂, b) existed, it would have to classify all four cases simultaneously. Each case imposes an inequality on the weights. Adding the two conditions for the cases with output 1 produces a result that directly contradicts the condition for (1,1).
replacements.no es que el optimizador no encuentre la: the optimizer is not merely failing to find a solution. There is no (w₁, w₂, b) that satisfies all four conditions. The impossibility is mathematical, not computational.
Two hidden neurons bend the space. The output boundary is still a straight line.
replacements.Cada neurona oculta traza su propia fron: Each hidden neuron draws its own boundary in the input space: one acts like OR (active if at least one input is 1) and another like AND (active only if both are 1). Together they create a band containing exactly the two XOR=1 cases. After projection into the new space, those two points collapse to the same position and a single straight line is enough.
replacements.(0,1) y (1,0) colapsan al mismo punto en: (0,1) and (1,0) collapse to the same point in the hidden space. The hidden layer does not classify: it transforms. The output neuron still draws a straight line, but in a space that the hidden layer has already bent.
